correctness.rationale: Exact finite procedures reconstruct the Franklin LCF graph and independently its six-by-six bipartite matrix, prove gamma_pr=6 by exhausting 66 size-two and 495 size-four subsets, and independently count 184 feasible size-six subsets. Every one of the 33,672 ordered distinct pairs was checked to have a valid target-improving exchange, proving the Johnson lower bound is attained. An independent BFS establishes all 16,836 unordered distances. The two standalone programs agree on 984 edges and the exact distance/eccentricity spectra, with an explicit non-matroid witness, and the LCF program enumerates all 48 automorphisms.

value.rationale: The Franklin graph is the uniquely extremal 12-vertex connected cubic bipartite graph for paired domination in the relevant published census, making its optimum-placement geometry a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The full metric equality for all pairs gives zero-detour optimal relocation even though the underlying family violates matroid basis exchange, separating a meaningful weak greedy exchange property from a stronger classical axiom. Complete distance/orbit profiles provide a compact exact reproducible benchmark; no unproved downstream theorem is asserted.
